payload.excerpt: What a honeymoon planner actually does from first call to coming home, the invisible work behind the bookings, and an honest view of when you need one.

key_takeaways: A honeymoon planner is a travel specialist who designs and books the trip and confirms in writing what is included; it is a service, not a printable planner.
The value sits in the invisible work: routing from Australia, transfers timed to checkout and check-in, matching rooms across stays and the handover from the wedding.
Upgrades, early check-in and late checkout are requests until they are confirmed in writing for your booking.
A planner earns its place on multi-stop, long-haul or tightly timed trips, especially straight after a wedding; for one hotel you already know, booking direct can be enough.
We suggest six to nine months for a honeymoon to lock in the right suite category.

faq.q: How much do honeymoon planners cost?
faq.a: There is no single figure: it depends on the planner and the trip. The fair standard is that any fee is agreed before work begins. For our own service: if any planning fee applies, you know before we start.

faq.q: How far in advance should we plan our honeymoon?
faq.a: Our wedding and honeymoon planning page suggests six to nine months for a honeymoon to lock in the right suite category. Leave room for documents too: Smartraveller suggests allowing at least six weeks to get a passport. For timing the trip itself, read about leaving straight after the wedding or waiting.

faq.q: What is a realistic honeymoon budget?
faq.a: There is no single right figure. It depends on the destination, the length of stay, the season and the suite category. Agree a range you are both comfortable with, decide what it covers, and compare how far a luxury budget goes in each destination.

faq.q: Can the same team plan our wedding and our honeymoon?
faq.a: Yes. The wedding and honeymoon can be one stay or two, or the same stay extended, with one specialist coordinating the whole trip.
